material.name: Cretaceous Field Documentary
material.style_instruction: Raw handheld natural-history field footage shot on location in a hot humid Late Cretaceous floodplain forest. Unprocessed documentary look: true-to-life colours, no grade, no colour filter, mild high-ISO grain crawling in the shadows, highlights that clip to flat white where the sun hits, shallow-depth background falloff with a soft bokeh that never looks painted. Subtropical haze softens everything past thirty metres; sweat, humidity and fine airborne grit sit in the air. Extinct animals are rendered to current palaeontological reconstruction standards with real animal skin physics: slack dewlaps, scar tissue, insect bites, caked red mud on the belly and feet, flies, laboured breathing that visibly moves the ribcage. Everything carries the weight and imperfection of real wildlife footage recorded by one person who is physically present and in danger.

material.lighting: Hot humid subtropical daylight filtered through palm and conifer canopy; hard dappled patches on the mud, heavy green bounce, thick haze in the depth, highlights clipping to white, no artificial fill
